purpose: Complete cutover map of every shipped or CI path that invokes or packages legacy Blueprint JS (blueprint/, blueprint/release/launchers/blueprint.cmd, runtime/blueprint/lib/node.exe), with native replacement and switch status, per NCL-03/NCL-02.
finding_summary: The source-level packaging/CI chain for the next release already does not stage or invoke the legacy Blueprint JS interpreter tree. RUNTIME_SPECS in runtime-inventory.mjs carries no Blueprint Node entry (blueprint-contract ships only the JSON schema resource; transport is a named-pipe to the native membrane-blueprint crate). package-portable-windows.mjs writes only a thin blueprint.cmd shim that execs membrane.exe. installer.nsi actively strips any legacy runtime/blueprint tree found under a version root and asserts (RemoveRetiredBlueprintRuntime, lines 367-372) that no node.exe/blueprint.cmd remain before completing install. The only place the legacy interpreter still ships is the CURRENTLY INSTALLED 0.1.24 product on this machine (an older signed release, pre-dating this cutover work) -- not something this lane can fix by editing scripts, since it requires a new signed installer build (out of lane scope; confirmed by scripts/qualification/cases/ncl-windows.mjs's own NCL-03 comment). No packaging/CI file edits were required to satisfy this lane's switch step because none of the entries below were still wired to the legacy interpreter.

entries.what_it_does_with_js: Declares RUNTIME_SPECS, the authoritative list of what the Tauri bundle ships. No entry names blueprint/, node.exe, or blueprint.cmd. The blueprint-contract entry ships only schemas/operations/membrane-blueprint.v1.schema.json (a JSON resource) with transport: named-pipe, pointing at the native membrane-blueprint crate surface.
entries.native_replacement: membrane.exe cli blueprint <op> (engine/crates/membrane-blueprint) reached over the named-pipe transport declared on the blueprint-contract spec.

entries.what_it_does_with_js: Stages RUNTIME_SPECS entries into src-tauri/runtime/. Contains zero references to blueprint/, node.exe, or .cmd launchers -- it only stages what runtime-inventory.mjs declares.
entries.native_replacement: N/A (staging script; nothing to switch, downstream of runtime-inventory.mjs)

entries.what_it_does_with_js: Copies the staged runtime/ tree (native-only per above) and writes a portable blueprint.cmd shim: `@echo off / "%~dp0membrane.exe" cli blueprint %* / exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%`. Also copies mcp/blueprint-readiness.mjs, which reads Blueprint freshness over a Unix-domain/named-pipe IPC socket (~/.blueprint/blueprint.sock) to the native daemon -- it never spawns node or the legacy blueprint.cmd.
entries.native_replacement: membrane.exe cli blueprint (invoked via the shim); blueprint-ipc named-pipe/socket protocol to the native daemon for readiness reads.

entries.what_it_does_with_js: Its only blueprint-related line is the same mcp/blueprint-readiness.mjs enrollment-file reference (native IPC client, see above); it does not build, stage, or invoke blueprint/ JS or node.exe.

Never adds runtime\blueprint to the package it builds. It actively removes any legacy runtime\blueprint tree found under a version root on upgrade/repair (RemoveRetiredBlueprintRuntime, invoked around lines 172-179 and step 330-335: 'remove-retired-blueprint-runtime'), then hard-asserts at lines 367-372 that $INSTDIR\versions\<version>\runtime\blueprint\lib\node.exe and \bin\blueprint.cmd do not exist, aborting install if they do.
entries.native_replacement: N/A (installer contains only cleanup/assertion logic against the legacy tree, not an invocation of it)

entries.what_it_does_with_js: Legacy launcher shims for the JS Blueprint CLI/MCP server, still present in the source tree under blueprint/release/launchers/. Not referenced by any packaging script above -- package-portable-windows.mjs synthesizes its own native blueprint.cmd shim at package time instead of copying this one.
entries.native_replacement: The synthesized native blueprint.cmd shim written by package-portable-windows.mjs (calls membrane.exe cli blueprint).
entries.can_switch_now: no (legacy source tree kept intentionally -- port parity not yet landed; not deleted per task instruction, and confirmed unreferenced by packaging)
entries.action_taken: none -- confirmed already unreferenced by any shipped/CI packaging path

This is a dev-only M0 baseline capture tool (not part of the shipped product or the release/installer path) whose purpose is to record the legacy JS suite's own baseline results for later parity comparison against the native port -- it deliberately targets the legacy suite as ground truth.

Once membrane-blueprint reaches full parity and blueprint/ is retired, this baseline command becomes historical and can be dropped from the active baseline set, but that is a port-parity-completion action, not a cutover-map switch.

cut2_addendum.purpose: CUT2 was dispatched to fully delete the legacy JS Blueprint tree and its remaining JS callers, on the premise that native parity had fully landed. Independent re-verification (rerunning the caller grep, reading CUT1/MCPHOST/PARMCP receipts dated the same day) shows that premise is false for a bounded set of items, so no deletion was performed.
cut2_addendum.reverified_caller_grep: grep -rln "blueprint/src|blueprint/release|mcp/host" --include=*.mjs --include=*.json --include=*.yml --include=*.md --include=*.cmd . | grep -v node_modules | grep -v "^./blueprint/" -> 104 hits, consistent with CUT1s prior pass; the overwhelming majority are historical audit/provenance docs (left untouched, per task scope) or generated evidence snapshots.
findings: CUT1 (lane-CUT1-2026-09-10.json) proved 3 qualification rows (BPT-018, BPT-020, BPT-026) have NO native equivalent in engine/crates/membrane-blueprint: comparePaths non-compensatory ranking (blueprint/src/graph/recall-circuit.mjs) and selective/incremental dependency-DAG invalidation (blueprint/src/graph/dependency-dag.mjs). Deleting blueprint/ would destroy the only implementation of behavior 3 qualification cases still depend on as fixture-level ground truth.

PARMCP (lane-PARMCP-2026-09-10.json) proved mcp/server.mjs (legacy JS MCP server) and package.json test/test:mcp/test:fable scripts still depend on mcp/host/*.test.mjs and 18 other mcp/*.test.mjs files with no native port; only a subset of mcp/host functionality has a native destination (per MCPHOST), and MCPHOSTs own host_context_adapter.rs port is explicitly partial (subprocess/HTTP transport and mcp/context-renderer-lib.cjs delegation excluded).
.github/workflows/ledger-completion.yml was grepped directly by CUT2 and contains zero blueprint/ or mcp/host references -- nothing to switch there.

scripts/run-m0-baseline-current.mjs and mcp/capability-inventory.mjs were re-confirmed by CUT2 to match CUT1s prior finding: both are intentionally legacy-targeting (baseline capture / provenance metadata) and not shipped/executed product behavior, so switching them now would misrepresent parity that does not exist yet for BPT-018/020/026.
cut2_addendum.action_taken: No deletion, no package.json/workflow/script edits. Retargeting package.json test/test:mcp/test:fable away from mcp/host would falsely claim coverage that PARMCP already proved does not exist (26 unported legacy test files). Marking migration/native-rust/runtime-policy.json exceptions closed or interpreter-dispositions.json rows deleted would fabricate a pass CUT1 explicitly declined to claim for the same reason.
cut2_addendum.recommendation: Re-run this lane only after a future lane lands (a) BPT-018/020/026 native parity in engine/crates/membrane-blueprint and (b) the remaining 26 mcp/mcp-host test ports plus mcp/server.mjs -> native membrane-mcp binary caller cutover. Until then blueprint/, mcp/host/, and mcp/server.mjs are not dead code and must not be removed.
